formation.title: The Rise of Tawantinsuyu
formation.text:
The four quarters of the world now bend to the will of a single Sapa Inca. From the frigid heights of the Altiplano to the steaming jungles of the Anti Suyu, from the arid coasts of the Kunti Suyu to the vast plains of the Qulla Suyu, the realm of the four parts stands united.

The transformation from a small kingdom in the Cusco valley into a continental empire demands a choice. Shall the Sapa Inca rule as the divine son of Inti, binding his people through religious fervor and military strength? Or shall he prove his mandate through masterful administration, weaving the disparate peoples of the Andes into a single prosperous state?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Children of the Sun!

modifiers.name: Children of Inti
modifiers.text: The Sapa Inca stands as the living son of the Sun, and his warriors march beneath the golden banner of Inti with unshakeable devotion. The empire's divine mandate inspires total commitment to the defense and expansion of Tawantinsuyu.

options.text: The Four Quarters shall prosper as one.

modifiers.name: Lords of the Four Quarters
modifiers.text: The genius of Tawantinsuyu lies not in conquest alone, but in the administration that follows. Through the mita labor system, the qullqa storehouses, and the quipu record-keepers, the Inca govern the largest empire in the Americas with remarkable efficiency.

advances.name: Qhapaq Nan
advances.text: The Great Inca Road, spanning over 30,000 kilometers across the Andes, enables rapid movement of armies, administrators, and trade goods throughout the empire.

advances.name: Ayllu Reciprocity
advances.text: The ayllu system of communal labor and mutual obligation forms the social bedrock of the Inca state, ensuring that no family faces hardship alone and that the state's demands are met through collective effort.

advances.name: Sapa Inca Divinity
advances.text: The Sapa Inca's status as the living son of Inti grants the empire's ruler unquestioned religious authority, reinforced through the construction of temples and the performance of sacred rituals.

advances.name: Qullqa Logistics
advances.text: The vast network of state storehouses along the Inca roads ensures that armies never go hungry, that provinces struck by disaster receive relief, and that the empire's surplus is distributed where it is needed most.

advances.name: Andean Metallurgy
advances.text: Andean peoples mastered the working of copper, tin, and their alloy bronze centuries before European contact. Inca metalworkers produced weapons, tools, and ceremonial objects of remarkable quality.

advances.name: Waru Waru
advances.text: The raised field farming technique of waru waru creates elevated planting surfaces surrounded by water channels, protecting crops from frost, improving drainage, and dramatically increasing yields in the challenging highland environment.

advances.name: Pachacuti Reforms
advances.text: The sweeping reorganization of the Inca state under Pachacuti (dividing the empire into four suyus, establishing the mita system, rebuilding Cusco, and codifying imperial law) transformed a regional kingdom into the greatest empire of the pre-Columbian Americas.

event.title: The Reforms of Pachacuti
event.text:
The great Sapa Inca Pachacuti (the Earthshaker, the World-Transformer) has remade the state from its foundations. What was once a modest kingdom centered on the Cusco valley has been reorganized into the vast Tawantinsuyu, the realm of the four quarters.

Pachacuti rebuilt Cusco in the shape of a puma, established the system of four suyus each governed by an apu, reformed the mita labor service into a tool of imperial construction, and codified the laws that bind a hundred conquered peoples into one empire. His military campaigns crushed the Chancas and extended Inca dominion across the Andes.

But will his legacy be remembered primarily as a conqueror who forged an empire through martial prowess, or as a builder whose administrative genius created the most organized state in the pre-Columbian Americas?

options.text: He shook the earth with his armies.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Earthshaker
modifiers.text: The military genius of Pachacuti inspires our commanders. His tactics of coordinated assault and psychological warfare echo through the ranks of Tawantinsuyu's armies.

options.text: He raised Cusco into a wonder of the world.

modifiers.name: Builder of Cusco
modifiers.text: Pachacuti's vision of a rebuilt Cusco (planned, ordered, magnificent) drives our architects and administrators to construct an empire worthy of the Sapa Inca.

advances.name: Anti Suyu Expansion
advances.text: The Inca conquest of the eastern jungle lowlands, the Anti Suyu, required developing entirely new military tactics. Lightweight infantry trained in jungle warfare became essential for operations in the dense tropical forests east of the Andes.

advances.name: Imperial Mita
advances.text: The expansion of the mita labor tax into a comprehensive system of state-directed labor enables the construction of roads, terraces, storehouses, and fortresses across the empire, turning every citizen into a builder of Tawantinsuyu.

advances.name: Capacocha Ritual
advances.text: The capacocha ceremony, the most sacred ritual of the Inca state, consecrates the empire's most important moments: the accession of a new Sapa Inca, great military victories, or times of crisis. Children from across the four suyus are brought to Cusco before returning to their home provinces, binding the periphery to the center through shared sacred experience.

advances.name: Yanacona Service
advances.text: The yanacona, servants of the state freed from ayllu obligations, form a dedicated class of administrators, artisans, and road-maintainers who serve the Sapa Inca directly, providing the empire with a loyal cadre of skilled professionals.

advances.name: Vilcabamba Resistance
advances.text: The Neo-Inca state at Vilcabamba survived for nearly four decades in the cloud forests, proving that Andean peoples could resist even the most powerful invaders by exploiting their knowledge of mountain terrain and guerrilla tactics.

event.title: The Retreat to Vilcabamba
event.text:
When foreign invaders seized Cusco and shattered the old order, the sons of the Sapa Inca did not surrender. Manco Inca retreated into the cloud forests of Vilcabamba, founding a Neo-Inca state that would resist for nearly forty years. From this remote mountain stronghold, the last Incas launched raids against the occupiers, maintained the old ceremonies, and kept the flame of Tawantinsuyu alive.

The spirit of Vilcabamba teaches two lessons. One is that mountains and jungle can shield a people from any invader, that guerrilla resistance can bleed an empire. The other is that survival sometimes demands adaptation: learning the enemy's language, adopting their useful tools, and finding allies among those who also resist.

modifiers.name: Spirit of Vilcabamba
modifiers.text: The defiance of the Neo-Inca state at Vilcabamba lives on. Our warriors know that the mountains themselves fight alongside them, and that no invader can hold what the Andes choose to reclaim.

options.text: We must learn from all who come.

modifiers.name: Diplomatic Adaptation
modifiers.text: The pragmatism of the Neo-Inca leaders (their willingness to learn foreign tongues, adopt useful technologies, and forge unexpected alliances) strengthens Tawantinsuyu's ability to navigate a changing world.

advances.name: Highland Gunpowder
advances.text: The adaptation of firearms to highland warfare demands different tactics than lowland combat. At altitude, sound carries further, powder burns differently, and the thin air affects both range and accuracy. Inca musketeers master these challenges through rigorous training in mountain conditions.

advances.name: Tocricuc Administration
advances.text: The tocricuc, provincial governors appointed by the Sapa Inca, serve as the eyes, ears, and hands of the central government in each corner of the empire. Their authority ensures that imperial decrees are carried out and local compliance is maintained.

advances.name: Silver Mountain
advances.text: The Andes contain some of the richest silver and precious metal deposits on earth. The development of advanced mining and smelting techniques transforms these mountain riches into the economic foundation of an imperial treasury.

advances.name: Inca Road Renewal
advances.text: The restoration and expansion of the ancient Qhapaq Nan road network ensures rapid communication and troop movement across the vast Andean terrain, binding the four quarters together as they were in the empire's golden age.

advances.name: Neo-Inca Reform
advances.text: Drawing on both ancient Inca traditions and modern military science, the reformed Tawantinsuyu creates disciplined standing forces capable of defending the highlands against any invader.

advances.name: Andean Textile Trade
advances.text: Highland wool and lowland cotton, woven in the obrajes of the Andes, become sought-after trade goods: qumpi, the fine cloth once reserved for the Sapa Inca's gifts, and awasqa, the plain cloth every household owed the state. The quality of Andean textiles, inheriting a tradition stretching back thousands of years, rivals the finest cloth of any civilization.

advances.name: Tupac Amaru Legacy
advances.text: The name Tupac Amaru echoes across the centuries: from the last emperor beheaded in Cusco's plaza to the great rebellion of 1780 that shook colonial rule to its foundations. As in that rising, the communities can be called out by their kurakas in the name of the Inca.

event.title: The Legacy of Tupac Amaru
event.text:
The name Tupac Amaru has become a rallying cry across the Andes. Whether it is the last Inca emperor executed by foreign conquerors in 1572, or the mestizo descendant who raised hundreds of thousands in revolt two centuries later, the name embodies the refusal of Andean peoples to accept subjugation.

Tupac Amaru II's rebellion of 1780 mobilized indigenous communities across Peru and Bolivia, shaking colonial rule to its foundations. His vision was of an Andean state free from foreign domination, where the old social structures would be restored and the dignity of the indigenous peoples upheld.

This legacy offers two paths: the fire of armed rebellion that would sweep away all foreign influence, or the patient work of building solidarity among all Andean peoples to create a state that draws strength from their shared heritage.

options.text: Let the fire of rebellion burn!

modifiers.name: Fire of Rebellion
modifiers.text: The revolutionary spirit of Tupac Amaru courses through our armies. Every soldier knows that they fight not merely for a king, but for the liberation of an entire people.

options.text: Our strength lies in our unity.

modifiers.name: Andean Solidarity
modifiers.text: The bonds between Andean communities (Quechua, Aymara, and all the peoples of the mountains) form the foundation of a state that draws its legitimacy from the shared heritage of a continent.

advances.name: Andean Terrace Renewal
advances.text: Ancient terrace systems are restored and expanded with modern agricultural knowledge, dramatically increasing food production across the highland regions and feeding a growing population.

advances.name: Mountain Artillery
advances.text: The placement of artillery in mountain passes and high-ground fortifications creates nearly impregnable defensive positions. No army can assault an Andean fortress without paying a terrible price in blood.

advances.name: Apu Governance
advances.text: The sacred apus, mountain spirits revered across the Andes, are invoked in the governance of each suyu. Provincial administrators draw legitimacy from their connection to these sacred peaks, blending spiritual authority with practical governance.

advances.name: Tawantinsuyu Restored
advances.text: The realm of the four quarters rises again with a modern army worthy of its ancient ambitions. Disciplined regiments trained in both highland and lowland warfare carry the banner of Tawantinsuyu into a new era.

advances.name: Andean Enlightenment
advances.text: The yachay wasi, houses of learning, spread literacy and knowledge throughout the Andes, producing a new generation of educated administrators, scientists, and philosophers who draw on both indigenous wisdom and the learning of the wider world.

advances.name: Industrial Andes
advances.text:
The rich mineral resources of the Andes (copper, tin, silver, gold) are processed with modern smelting techniques, transforming the mountains into the industrial heartland of a resurgent Tawantinsuyu.

Available in: Mita Workshop

advances.name: Inti Raymi Revival
advances.text: The great Festival of the Sun, the Inti Raymi, is revived as the supreme cultural celebration of Tawantinsuyu, drawing pilgrims from across the four quarters to Cusco for nine days of ceremony, feasting, and renewal of the empire's divine mandate.

advances.name: Modern Chasqui
advances.text: The ancient relay runner system that once carried messages across the Andes at remarkable speed is modernized with postal stations, signal towers, and organized courier networks, ensuring that the Sapa Inca's word reaches every corner of the realm without delay.

advances.name: Sovereign Andes
advances.text: The Andes stand as a sovereign power, its armies disciplined, its people united, its mountains unconquered. The children of the Sun have reclaimed their destiny and forged a state that no foreign power can subjugate.

destiny.name: Destiny of Tawantinsuyu
destiny.text: The Inca Empire stands restored. With the four quarters united under a single Sapa Inca, the time has come to fulfill the greater destiny of Tawantinsuyu: whether through divine conquest or masterful administration.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Destiny of Tawantinsuyu
event.text: The four quarters stand united once more, and the Sapa Inca's gaze turns toward the horizon. What began as a restoration of ancient glory now demands a greater vision: a destiny worthy of Inti's chosen people. The path forward will define whether Tawantinsuyu is remembered as the mightiest empire of the Americas, or as the most brilliantly administered state the world has ever seen.

destiny.name: Masters of the Coast
destiny.text: The great coastal kingdoms of Chan Chan and Arequipa must submit to the will of the Sapa Inca. These ancient centers are conquered, and tambos, the stocked way stations of the royal road, are built in three places to feed the host on its march to the sea.

Own Chan Chan, or a subject owns it
Own Arequipa, or a subject owns it
A Tambo stands in at least 3 of our locations

event.title: The Coastal Kingdoms Submit
event.text:
The great adobe cities of the coast (Chan Chan of the Chimu, the terraced settlements of Arequipa) now fly the banner of Tawantinsuyu. Where once independent kingdoms controlled the rich fishing grounds and irrigated valleys of the Pacific shore, now the Sapa Inca's authority extends from the mountain peaks to the ocean itself.

The conquest of the coast gives Tawantinsuyu access to resources that the highlands alone could never provide: marine wealth, irrigated cotton fields, and the strategic depth of a two-front empire.

options.text: The coast bends to the will of Inti.

destiny.name: The Four Quarters Extended
destiny.text: The borders of Tawantinsuyu are pressed to their natural limits. The northern frontier must reach Quito, and the southern Altiplano centered on sacred Tiwanaku must acknowledge the Sapa Inca's dominion. Willkawaman, which stands on the royal road as far from Quito as from the southern frontier, is built up as the middle of the realm. Tambos stand in six places along the roads the armies take.

conditions.text: Own Quitu, or a subject owns it
Own Tiwanaku, or a subject owns it
A Tambo stands in at least 6 of our locations
We own Willkawaman and its development is at least 10

event.title: Expansion of the Four Quarters
event.text:
With Quito secured in the north and sacred Tiwanaku brought under the eagle banner in the south, Tawantinsuyu has grown beyond the wildest dreams of the earliest Sapa Incas. The empire now spans climatic zones from equatorial heat to the frigid Altiplano.

This vast expansion demands a choice in how the empire sustains its military power. Shall the Sapa Inca prioritize rapid mobilization of new armies from the conquered territories, or develop an intelligence network to anticipate threats before they materialize?

modifiers.name: Rapid Mobilization
modifiers.text: The mita labor system is adapted into a military draft that can raise armies across the four quarters with extraordinary speed, though the diversion of labor from trade weakens merchant networks.

modifiers.name: Imperial Scouts
modifiers.text: The chasqui relay runner network is repurposed as an intelligence apparatus, carrying reports of enemy movements and foreign intrigues across the Andes at remarkable speed.

destiny.name: Empire of the Sun
destiny.text: The supreme achievement of Inti's children: a continental empire stretching from Tumbes on the Pacific coast to the Atacama frontier at Arica, with Chuqiyapu secured in the heartland, and ordered into four suyus as Pachacuti's reforms laid down. No force on earth can challenge Tawantinsuyu.

conditions.text: Own Tumbes, or a subject owns it
Own Arica, or a subject owns it
Own Chuqiyapu, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000
Discovery or later

event.title: Empire of the Sun Ascendant
event.text:
From Tumbes in the tropical north to the arid frontier at Arica, from the highland capital at Qusqu to the Altiplano stronghold of Chuqiyapu, Tawantinsuyu has achieved what no other American state has accomplished: continental dominion under a single divine ruler.

This supreme achievement demands a doctrine for maintaining eternal supremacy. Shall the empire adopt a posture of perpetual readiness for total war, crushing any threat before it can grow? Or shall it fortify its mountain strongholds into an impregnable defensive network, making any invasion of the Andes suicidal?

options.text: We shall crush all who defy us.

modifiers.name: Total War Doctrine
modifiers.text: The empire adopts a doctrine of permanent readiness for war, maintaining mercenary reserves and accelerating campaigns at the cost of increased borrowing to sustain the war economy.

options.text: The mountains are our eternal shield.

modifiers.name: Mountain Fortress Doctrine
modifiers.text: The Andes themselves become a weapon. Mountain passes are fortified, garrison networks expanded, and intelligence operations hardened, making any invasion of Tawantinsuyu prohibitively costly.

destiny.name: The Quipu Economy
destiny.text: The genius of Inca administration was its ability to manage a vast economy without currency or writing. Now the treasury is filled while the redistributive spirit of the quipu system is kept. Ensure silver flows through the capital markets.

event.title: The Quipu Counts True
event.text:
The quipucamayocs, the keepers of the knotted cords, have long managed the most complex economy in the pre-Columbian Americas without written language or minted currency. Now, as silver and markets take root in the Andes, the administrative genius of the quipu system learns to keep the accounts of a market economy.

Silver from the mountain mines flows through the capital markets, and the redistributive tradition of the Inca state adapts to the demands of a monetized economy. The result is something unprecedented: an empire that combines the social safety net of communal redistribution with the dynamism of market exchange.

options.text: The quipu and the coin serve one master.

destiny.name: The Provincial Capitals
destiny.text: Capitals are raised in the provinces in the image of Qusqu, each with its plaza, its hall of feasts and its sun temple, where the lords of the province are received and given their tasks. Hatun Xauxa, the capital of the Mantaro valley, is built up, and the realm's renown grows with it.

conditions.text: We own Hatun Xauxa and its development is at least 13
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Provincial Capitals Raised
event.text:
Along the royal road stand cities that no province built for itself. Each is laid out in the image of Qusqu around a plaza wide enough to hold a province, with a platform from which the governor speaks for the Sapa Inca. Here the lords of the conquered peoples are feasted with maize beer and cloth from the state's stores, and here they are told what labour their people owe.

These cities can serve different purposes. Their plazas may become the fairs of an Andean market that draws merchants from across the continent, or they may serve first as courts of hospitality, extending the reach of Tawantinsuyu's influence far beyond its borders.

options.text: Let the markets flourish in every plaza.

modifiers.name: Andean Market Integration
modifiers.text: The plazas of the provincial capitals become the backbone of a continent-spanning market system. Merchant capacity expands, inflation stabilizes, and even the smallest ayllu benefits from guaranteed minimum trade revenue.

options.text: Our roads carry influence as well as goods.

modifiers.name: Road Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The Qhapaq Nan road network extends Tawantinsuyu's diplomatic reach far beyond its borders, enabling embassies and trade missions to distant lands, though the outward focus leaves garrison forces stretched thin.

destiny.name: Heart of the Four Suyus
destiny.text: The culmination of Tawantinsuyu's administrative genius: a state so prosperous and well-governed that it becomes the economic heart of the continent. Qusqu, the navel of the four suyus, is built up, wealth is accumulated, and gold flows through the empire's markets.

event.title: Heart of the Four Suyus
event.text:
Tawantinsuyu has achieved what the Sapa Inca Pachacuti could only have dreamed: an empire so wealthy, so efficiently governed, and so deeply rooted in the knowledge of both ancient Andean traditions and modern science that it stands as the economic heart of an entire continent.

Gold and silver flow through the empire's markets. The quipucamayocs now work alongside trained administrators, and the yachay wasi schools of Qusqu teach a new generation. Two visions of the future present themselves: continental hegemony through diplomatic and economic dominance, or a perfected redistributive state that becomes a model for all civilizations.

modifiers.name: Continental Hegemon
modifiers.text: Tawantinsuyu stands as the unchallenged economic and diplomatic power of the continent, its prestige attracting vassals and its administrators skilled at incorporating conquered peoples.

options.text: The state shall provide for all.

modifiers.name: The Redistributive State
modifiers.text: The ancient Inca principle of redistribution is perfected: taxes are collected fairly, cities grow organically, and every citizen advances through merit. The state provides, and the people prosper.

units.name: Runa Infantry
units.text: Conscripted through the mita labor system, runa infantry form the backbone of the Inca army. These common soldiers bring mountain-hardened endurance and unwavering loyalty to the service of the Sapa Inca.

units.name: Inca Slingers
units.text: Trained from childhood in the highland villages, Inca slingers can hurl stones with devastating accuracy at speeds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour. Their ranged volleys soften enemy formations before the main assault begins.

units.name: Anti Suyu Warriors
units.text: Specialists in jungle warfare, these light infantry are recruited from the eastern frontier of the empire. They excel at ambushes, rapid movement through dense vegetation, and fighting in terrain where heavy formations cannot operate.

units.name: Highland Musketeers
units.text: Trained to handle firearms at altitude where powder burns differently and thin air affects ballistics, highland musketeers combine the accuracy demanded by mountain warfare with the devastating firepower of gunpowder weapons.

units.name: Mountain Guard
units.text: Elite defenders of the Andean passes, the Mountain Guard are trained to hold positions against overwhelming odds. Their knowledge of highland terrain, combined with modern equipment and iron discipline, makes them formidable in defensive engagements.

units.name: Tawantinsuyu Regiment
units.text: The premier fighting force of the restored Inca Empire, these regiments combine ancient Andean martial traditions with modern military science. They fight with equal proficiency in mountain passes and open plains.

units.name: Tupamaros
units.text: The communities of the highlands, called out by their kurakas in the name of the Inca as in the rising of 1780. Slingers and lancers in their thousands with few muskets among them, they are not easily scattered and suffer heavily under fire.

buildings.name: Coricancha
buildings.text: The Temple of the Sun, its walls once sheathed in gold, serves as the spiritual heart of Tawantinsuyu. Within its precincts, the Willaq Umu and his priests maintain the sacred fires and perform the rituals that bind the empire to its divine patron.

buildings.name: Imperial Qullqa
buildings.text: State storehouses filled with dried potatoes, maize, quinoa, and military supplies. The qullqa network ensures that no province faces famine and that armies can be fed during any campaign, embodying the redistributive genius of the Inca economy.

buildings.name: Mita Workshop
buildings.text: A state-organized workshop where mita laborers produce goods under imperial direction. Metalwork, masonry, and weaving are carried out with the efficiency of organized labor, transforming raw materials into the tools of empire.

buildings.name: Silver Foundry
buildings.text: Rows of huayra wind furnaces on the ridges above a silver or copper mine. Fired with charcoal and llama dung when the evening wind rises, they smelt the ore where it is dug, and the mines below yield more.

children.text: The location's raw material is Silver
The location's raw material is Copper

buildings.name: Andean Obraje
buildings.text: A highland textile workshop producing fine cloth from llama and alpaca wool. Andean weaving traditions, stretching back thousands of years, produce textiles of extraordinary quality that command premium prices in markets across the known world.

buildings.name: Yachay Wasi
buildings.text: A house of learning where the knowledge of the Andes (astronomy, agriculture, medicine, engineering, and governance) is taught alongside the learning of the wider world. The yachay wasi preserves and transmits the intellectual heritage of Tawantinsuyu.

buildings.name: Inti Huasi Wamani
buildings.text: The House of the Sun's War: a sacred military complex where warriors receive the blessing of Inti before marching to battle. Within its walls, commanders plan campaigns under golden sun discs, and soldiers train among altars where offerings ensure divine victory.

buildings.name: Hatun Qhatu
buildings.text: The great market of a provincial capital, held in the open plaza beside the royal road under the eye of the Inca's officers. Maize and coca from the valleys, salt and dried fish from the coast and wool from the high pastures change hands here, and the stores behind the plaza feed the crowd on the days of the fair.

list.name: Willaq Umu and the Priesthood of the Sun
list.text: The Willaq Umu, the priest who speaks, stood at the head of the cult of Inti and was by custom a brother or uncle of the Sapa Inca. He held the office for life, named the priests of the Sun in every province and kept the calendar of the state festivals from the Coricancha in Cuzco. In each conquered province fields and herds were set apart for the Sun and worked by the ayllus in their turn, and their harvest fed the feasts at which the ruler was shown to his people as the son of Inti. A priesthood that answered to the ruler's own kin made his descent a matter of doctrine. Left unprovided, it left the feasts unheld and the lords of Cuzco without their place in them.

conditions.text: Inti religion

list.name: Tawantinsuyu Four-Suyu Governorate
list.text: The empire's name was Tawantinsuyu, meaning the four united regions: Chinchaysuyu to the northwest, Antisuyu in the eastern montana, Collasuyu reaching south to the Maule, and Cuntisuyu running to the Pacific coast. Each suyu was governed by an Apu drawn from the close kin of the Sapa Inca, who coordinated the provincial Tucuyricoc royal inspectors and supervised the curaca local lords below them. The four-suyu division turned the conquered Andean realms into a single intelligible administrative geometry centered on the central plaza of Cuzco, the navel of the world.

list.name: Quipucamayoc Record-Keepers
list.text: The empire ran without writing on knotted cords called quipus, whose plies, colors, knot-types, and knot-positions encoded census data, tribute assignments, mit'a rotations, and dynastic chronology. The Quipucamayoc were specialist administrators trained in the yachay wasi schools at Cuzco, drawn from noble families and from the children of conquered curacas; only they could read the cords. The system tracked the population of every ayllu in the realm at decimal granularity (decuria, century, half-thousand, thousand) and was the indispensable backbone of every Inca tax assignment, labour roll, and military muster.

list.name: Mit'a Rotational Labour Levy
list.text: Every adult male of the conquered ayllus owed the Sapa Inca a fixed rotation of labour each year: on state lands, in the Potosi-region mines, on the Qhapaq Nan road, in the royal granaries of Cuzco and Quito, and in seasonal military service. A separate caste of Yanakuna provided full-time palace and elite servants outside the rotation. The mit'a delivered the workforce that built Sacsayhuaman, Machu Picchu, and the entire imperial road network in less than a century, but it was an obligation owed by the ayllu rather than the individual, and grew brutal where the rotation fell on a community already depleted by drought or war.

list.name: Mitma Resettlement System
list.text: When a region resisted incorporation or held strategic value, the Inca state moved entire populations. Loyal Quechua-speaking ayllus from the Cuzco heartland were transplanted into the conquered territory, and the conquered population was, in turn, broken into fragments and settled across the empire from the Atacama coast to the Ecuadorian sierra. The mitma simultaneously diluted local ethnic cohesion, spread the imperial Quechua language, and gave each rebellious zone a counterweight of crown-loyal settlers. It was the most aggressive instrument of Andean state-formation and it left a permanent demographic fingerprint visible in the modern distribution of Quechua across western South America.

list.name: Acllahuasi
list.text: The House of the Chosen Women, where daughters of provincial curacas selected for their beauty and lineage were cloistered from age ten to weave qompi cloth for the Sapa Inca, brew chicha for the state festivals of Inti, and serve as priestesses in the temples of the sun. A few became secondary wives of the emperor; most became mamacuna, permanent religious specialists serving the cult for life. The institution doubled as a hostage system (a curaca whose daughter served in the Acllahuasi of Cuzco was a curaca whose loyalty was guaranteed) and as the state's principal manufacturer of fine textiles, the most important non-food good in the entire Andean economy.

conditions.text: Inti religion

list.name: Chakakamayuq, Keepers of the Bridges
list.text: The royal road crosses the gorges of the Andes on hanging bridges of twisted grass rope, the longest of them over the Apurimac. Each bridge is the charge of a chakakamayuq, a keeper drawn with his helpers from the villages nearby, who owe the work as their mit'a. Every year the villages twist new cables and hang the bridge afresh; every day the keeper watches who crosses and with what load, and nobody passes without the state's leave. Armies and llama trains cross a kept bridge in a morning. A bridge left one season without new rope falls into the river, and the province beyond it is a province alone.
